find / -path "*/packages/server/src/i18n*" -not -path "*/node_modules/*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | head -30
echo "---"
find / -path "*@guren/core*" -iname "*.d.ts" 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -l "useTranslation\|I18nManager\|class Controller" 2>/dev/null | head -10

result:
Everything checks out. Summary of the change:

I added a Japanese locale to the i18n system and moved the login/register page copy into translation catalogs. `src/app.ts` now declares `i18n: { supported: ['en', 'ja'] }`. New catalog files `lang/en/auth.json` and `lang/ja/auth.json` hold the `auth.login.*`/`auth.register.*` keys (title, heading, subtitle, field labels, submit button, footer question/link) with the exact English and Japanese strings from the spec, and `lang/ja/messages.json` adds the Japanese welcome message (`:nameへようこそ！`) alongside the existing English one, preserving the `:name` placeholder. `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx` and `Register.tsx` were rewired to pull every visible string (including the `<Head>` title) from `useTranslation()` instead of hardcoded JSX text, and `LoginController.ts`/`RegisterController.ts` now pass `this.t('auth.login.title')`/`this.t('auth.register.title')` as the server-rendered document title. Ran `bunx guren codegen` (regenerating `.guren/translations.gen.ts` with 20 typed keys) and `bunx guren check`, which confirms both `lang/en` and `lang/ja` cover all 20 keys with no drift. Verified with a scratch `TestApp` request that an `Accept-Language: ja` request resolves `<title>ログイン</title>` and shares the full `ja`/`en` message catalogs via the `_i18n` Inertia prop (used by `useTranslation()` at render time), while a request with no `Accept-Language` header still renders the English strings. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass.
